sections.title: Advanced Strategy for Level 3
sections.content: At Level 3, the relationships between figures are often hidden across multiple layers. Step 1: Observe the entire structure such as grids, matrices, or unfolding patterns. Step 2: Identify rules across both rows and columns. Step 3: Look for mathematical or logical relationships between elements such as addition or removal of lines. Step 4: Understand each transformation step in sequence. Step 5: Apply the same rule to determine the missing figure.

sections.title: 3×3 Figure Matrix Analogies
sections.content: In a 3×3 grid, figures change across both rows and columns. Step 1: Identify the relationship among the three figures in the first row. Step 2: Check whether the same rule applies in the second row. Step 3: Observe patterns across the columns as well. Step 4: Sometimes two shapes combine to form the third, or common lines are removed. Step 5: Combine both row and column patterns to identify the missing figure.

sections.title: Mathematical Combination of Shapes
sections.content: In many matrix questions, shapes are combined mathematically. Step 1: Observe the shapes in Column 1 and Column 2. Step 2: Identify common lines or shapes. Step 3: Common elements may cancel out or combine to create a new figure. Step 4: The resulting shape appears in Column 3. Step 5: Apply the same rule to determine the missing figure.

sections.title: 3D Proxy Classification (Cube Folding)
sections.content: Some questions provide unfolded cube nets. Step 1: Identify faces and symbols on each net. Step 2: Determine which faces will become opposite when folded. Step 3: Visualize which faces will be adjacent when the cube is formed. Step 4: If three nets form the same cube, their symbol arrangements will match. Step 5: The net that forms a different cube is the odd one out.

sections.title: Sequential Progressive Analogies
sections.content: In some questions, figures change through multiple steps. Step 1: Compare the first and second steps. Step 2: Identify movements or transformations such as rotation, shifting, or addition. Step 3: Check whether the rule remains constant or progresses with each step. Step 4: Extend the pattern logically to find the missing step. Step 5: Select the figure that correctly completes the sequence.

sections.title: Grid-Based Movement Patterns
sections.content: In grid-based problems, elements move from one position to another. Step 1: Identify grid positions such as top-left, center, or bottom-right. Step 2: Observe the direction in which the element moves at each step. Step 3: Movement may be linear, diagonal, or circular. Step 4: Determine the logical next position based on the pattern.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Observing only rows or only columns instead of both. 2. Misinterpreting opposite faces in cube nets. 3. Ignoring the sequence of steps in movement patterns. 4. Partially understanding combination rules.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 reasoning is multi-layered. In matrix analogies, analyze patterns across both rows and columns. In cube classification, understand the logic of folding and opposite faces. In sequential analogies, follow the movement pattern step by step to identify the missing figure.

tricks.title: Row–Column Rule
tricks.explanation: In a 3×3 matrix, observe patterns across both rows and columns.
tricks.example: Shapes may increase in rows while rotation occurs in columns.

tricks.title: Shape Combination Trick
tricks.explanation: Two shapes may combine to form a third shape or common parts may disappear.
tricks.example: A square and a triangle combine to form a new outline.

tricks.title: Common Line Cancellation
tricks.explanation: When shapes overlap, common lines may cancel out.
tricks.example: Two identical lines overlap and disappear, forming a new shape.

tricks.title: Cube Opposite Face Rule
tricks.explanation: In cube nets, faces that are not adjacent in a straight layout may become opposite when folded.
tricks.example: The top face will be opposite the bottom face.

tricks.title: Adjacency Check
tricks.explanation: Adjacent faces in a cube will touch each other when folded.
tricks.example: The front face will touch the left and right faces.

tricks.title: Sequential Movement Rule
tricks.explanation: If an element moves one position in each step, the same pattern continues.
tricks.example: A dot moves clockwise in every step.

tricks.title: Identify Diagonal Movement
tricks.explanation: In grid sequences, elements may move diagonally.
tricks.example: From top-left to center and then to bottom-right.

tricks.title: Progressive Rotation
tricks.explanation: The rotation angle may increase with each step.
